From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: multi-region performance discussion and proposed tests

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move into a hands-on comparison window quickly: 

Summary of what you asked for:
- Objective: quantify regional latency / throughput differences for your real workload across US, EU, and APAC while preserving strict data residency for EU data.
- Comparison baseline: you want us to test Redwood inference against your current hyperscaler setup (same model family, same prompt mix, same token budget) to surface p50/p95 latency, token cost, and tail behavior.
- Security/compliance: Procurement & Security will need an exportable evidence bundle (audit logs, retention certs).

Proposed next tests (my suggested order):
1) Smoke run (48h): small traffic (50 rps) from three regions to validate endpoints and KV cache priming.
2) Latency sweep: synthetic and real prompts, measure p50/p90/p95 and cold-start distribution across regions.
3) Throughput test: step up to target qps (your target: 200 qps) while tracking request queuing and token cost.
4) Hyperscaler parity run: copy the same model and prompt mix (we'll use a 13B quantized variant where applicable) and run side-by-side with your current endpoint for a 24h window.
5) Data residency verification: demonstrate that EU-submitted payloads land in eu-west and confirm log retention behavior.

What I need from you to kick off:
- A list of sample prompt templates and a small representative dataset (1000 prompt examples).
- Any IP/data residency constraints we should encode in routing.
- Point of contact for Procurement/Security (or introduce them on reply).
- Windows for running the parity test (preferred: overnight your timezone to minimize production interference).

Attachments: I can prepare a short test plan doc and a preliminary checklist — will attach in the next message.

If this looks right I can loop in Ben (infrastructure lead) and Dylan (benchmarks) and we’ll share a concrete schedule and temporary endpoints.

Thanks again — excited to get you measurable numbers.

—Marissa
